indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.3.3.1: Show understanding and appreciation of the interactions and interdependencies of organisms in an ecosystem
indicator.objective: Identify organisms in a habitat and describe why they live in a particular place

skills.description: Identify organisms in a given habitat
Identify observable features that help organisms live there
Explain why an organism lives in a particular place
Give examples of organisms and their habitats

misconceptions: All animals can live in any habitat.
A fish can live on land if it is wet.
Plants are not part of a habitat.
Birds live only in the air and never on land.
A frog is a fish because it lives in water.

questions.stem: Where does a fish live?
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water (a water habitat).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish can live on land.

questions.stem: Where does a bird usually live?
questions.explanation: Birds live in trees (land habitat) and fly in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think birds only live in the air.

questions.stem: Where does a goat live?
questions.explanation: A goat lives on land.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all animals live in water.

questions.stem: Where do grasshoppers usually live?
questions.explanation: Grasshoppers live in grassy areas on land.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think grasshoppers live in water.

questions.stem: What feature helps a fish swim in water?
hints: They are on the side of its body.
They help it move through water.
questions.explanation: Fins are the features that help a fish swim and balance in water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish use legs to move.

questions.stem: What feature helps a bird fly in the air?
questions.explanation: Wings are the features that allow a bird to fly in the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think birds fly using fins.

questions.stem: What feature helps a frog swim in water?
hints: It has skin between its toes.
questions.explanation: A frog has webbed feet, which act like paddles to help it swim.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think frogs swim like fish with fins.

questions.stem: What feature helps a cow eat grass?
questions.explanation: Cows have flat teeth suitable for grinding grass and plants.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think cows have sharp teeth like lions.

questions.stem: Why does a fish live in water?
options: It needs water to breathe and swim
It is afraid of the land
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water because it uses gills to breathe and fins to swim. It cannot survive on land.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish just prefer water but could live on land.

questions.stem: Why do birds live in trees?
options: Trees provide shelter, safety, and a place to build nests
They are afraid of the ground
hints: Where do they lay their eggs?
Trees keep them safe from some predators.
questions.explanation: Birds live in trees because trees offer shelter, a safe place for their nests, and protection.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think birds live in trees because they are made of wood.

questions.stem: Why do grasshoppers live in grass?
options: The grass provides food and camouflage (hiding)
questions.explanation: Grasshoppers live in grass because they eat it and their green colour helps them hide from predators.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think they live in grass for no reason.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of a habitat?
hints: It is a natural place where living things live.
questions.explanation: A pond is an example of a natural habitat where fish, frogs, and water plants live.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any place is a habitat.

questions.stem: Why can a fish NOT live on land?
options: It does not have legs to walk, and it cannot breathe air
questions.explanation: A fish lacks legs for walking and uses gills to breathe in water. It cannot survive out of water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a fish can breathe on land if it is wet.

questions.stem: A tilapia has fins and gills. How are these features suited to its habitat?
options: Fins help it swim, and gills help it breathe in water
Fins help it fly, and gills help it eat
Fins help it walk, and gills help it run
Fins help it climb, and gills help it jump
hints: How does it move? How does it breathe?
questions.explanation: Tilapia lives in water; its fins help it swim, and its gills extract oxygen from the water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the function of fins and gills.

questions.stem: Why does a frog live near a pond or stream?
options: It needs water to lay eggs, but also land to catch insects
It needs to drink water every minute
hints: Frogs start their lives as tadpoles in water.
Adult frogs catch insects on land.
questions.explanation: Frogs need water for breeding and laying eggs, but as adults, they live on land to catch insects.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think frogs are completely aquatic like fish.

questions.stem: After heavy rain, earthworms often come to the surface of the soil. Why do they live in the soil?
options: The soil is moist, and they can burrow for safety
They come up to drink water
They want to see the sun
hints: Where do they make their homes?
questions.explanation: Earthworms live in soil because it provides moisture and protection. When it rains, the soil gets too wet, forcing them up.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think worms come up because they like the light.

questions.stem: What feature helps a bird to catch insects in the air?
hints: It uses this to grab food.
questions.explanation: Birds have beaks adapted for catching and eating their specific types of food (e.g., insects).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think feet are used for catching food in the air.

questions.stem: Why can a camel survive in a hot desert, but not in a rainforest?
options: It is adapted to survive with very little water and extreme heat, which it would not find in a rainforest
It is too big for the rainforest
questions.explanation: Camels are adapted to dry, hot conditions. In a wet rainforest, they would suffer from the moisture and different environment.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any animal can survive anywhere.

questions.stem: Why do different organisms live in different habitats?
options: Because they have different features adapted to survive in specific conditions
Because they are afraid of each other
questions.explanation: Organisms live in habitats where their physical features and needs (food, water, shelter) are best met.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think habitat choice is random.

questions.stem: A frog has webbed feet and a fish has fins. Explain how BOTH features are suited to living in water.
options: Both features act like paddles to help them move through water
They are not suited to water
questions.explanation: Webbed feet and fins both increase the surface area, acting as paddles to propel the animals through water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the analogy between a frog's foot and a fish's fin.
